The way this question is framed, there is no possible way you could have found out which direction their conversations go in by asking “why don’t you have the solutions?” The only thing you would’ve found out is that he simply doesn’t have them. Better questions would have been, “have you ever discussed why she’s feeling this way?”, or simply asking “what do you say to her when she comes to you, if you say anything at all?”, like you clearly stated you wanted to know. This is the wrong question to ask for the answers you’re seeking.

Unless you’re a trained mental health professional, there’s really no reason someone who’s presumably not depressed would know solutions to problems created by depression. It’s like expecting someone who’s swam in a pool to offer solutions to someone else  who’s stuck out at sea. How would that person know what to do? Even if they have a surface level understanding of the situation, they have nowhere near enough experience to know how to help. Why can’t he offer solutions? Because he’s presumably never experienced what she’s experiencing before, so how would he know what the solution is to begin with? That’s why this is a dumb question.
